overview.description: Danish Tarok (Grosstarock) is a three-player trick-taking game using a 78-card tarot deck (21 trumps, Fool, 4 suits of 14). Primary objective: win the last trick with the lowest trump (trump 1) or a King. Secondary: win tricks and capture counting cards. Alliances form during play. Each player gets 25 cards (dealer gets 3 extra then discards to 25). Declarations at start: trump holdings, matadors (Fool, lowest trump, 21), court combinations. Two pots (king pot, lowest-trump pot). Card values: 4 for trump 21, lowest trump, Fool, Kings; 3 Queens; 2 Knights; 1 Jacks. Closely related to German Grosstarock; survives mainly in Denmark.

history.origins: Danish Tarok is the surviving form of German Grosstarock (Grosstarok), introduced in Germany around 1720; now played mainly in Denmark. 78-card tarot, 3 players, lowest-trump/King ultimo and two pots.
timeline: 20th century: Survives in Denmark as Danish Tarok

setup.players: Three active players. With four people, the player opposite the dealer sits out and does not play; that player shuffles the spare pack. Play is counter-clockwise; the player to the dealer's right leads to the first trick.
setup.dealing: 25 cards each; dealer gets 3 extra then discards to 25

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trumps rank 21 high to 1 low; Fool is excuse and does not win tricks.

edgeCases.text: Fool can be played anytime; when led, player names the suit; Fool never wins a trick and goes to the player's trick pile except in the last trick when it goes to the winner.
Fool must never be played to the second-to-last trick.
In the third-to-last trick, any player without the Fool may require that it be played; play is taken back as necessary.
Ultimo: win last trick with Pagat or a King for bonus; Bagud: play Pagat or King to last trick and lose for penalty.
Tout: one player takes all 25 tricks; Nolo: one player takes no tricks.
Dealer may not discard Ultimo cards, Mondo, or cards that are part of declarations (with rare exceptions).

customActions.description: Dealer deals five cards at a time to each player until each has 25; dealer receives three extra then discards to skat.
Dealer discards three cards to the skat; Ultimo cards, Mondo, and declared combinations may not be discarded except under specific rules.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; after receiving 28 cards; must leave 25 in hand.

engine.handRankingSystem: Trick ranking: highest trump wins; if no trump, highest card in led suit. Fool is excuse and does not win tricks. Trumps rank 21 high to 1 low.
engine.deckDescription: A 78-card French-suited historical tarock deck with 21 numbered trumps plus the Fool and four French suits used for older Alpine tarock games.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits: Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs. Trumps are permanent and separate from the suit cards.
engine.rankDescription: Suit cards use tarot courts King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack with numeral cards 10 down to 1. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Fool.
engine.dealPattern: Five cards at a time to each of the three players until each has 25; dealer receives three extra cards then discards three to the skat.
